reason: Monostromatic means one cell layer thick, a count of cell layers (cf. distromatic). PATO:0002069 unstratified is a tissue-layering quality and too loose a match.
'Terminated by a bristle' is aristate, which the previous review mapped to awn present (rules C168, C207).
A bur-like fruit or head is covered with stiff, often hooked prickles. The broader PATO spiny is safer than FLOPO barbed, because the hooks are not always stated.

label: callus-tipped
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's apex ending in a small, hard, thickened callus. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991210 spine-tipped; the callus need not be sharp, so the class is not placed under PATO:0002258 pointed.
reason: Leaf apices and teeth with a hardened callus tip are a standard botanical character with no PATO or FLOPO term. 'Callus' alone was rejected as a generic part, so the quality is needed.
'Seeds minutely decorated' means the surface is sculptured, which is PATO ornamented (a surface with ridges, pits or other structures).
A relation of the sepal to another part (PATO:0001772 surrounding, EXACT synonym enclosing, is relational), here negated.
'With glandular dots' means gland-dotted; 'without glandular dots' is its negation.
It states that the bearer has bracts and that the bracts are leaf-like: bract (PO_0009055) leaf-like (PATO_0002457), as a part of the bearer. It is not one quality of the inflorescence.
Leaves in many ranks (more than 2 or 3 rows) means spiral phyllotaxis with many rows. The few-ranked cases are PATO distichous and tristichous.
Two values: the part is multi-coloured (PATO_0001533) and the marking is yellow (PATO_0000324), often at a stated region (the throat). One term would hide the marking colour.
'Blades with evident midnerves' means a midvein is present (midrib is an EXACT synonym). On stipules the bearer should be vascular bundle (PO_0005020) instead.
A count of trunks (stem PO_0009047) of more than one per plant, like 'few-flowered'. It is a count, not a quality term.
Root-sprouting means producing suckers from the roots, and PO lists sucker as a synonym of root-borne shoot system. 'Not' makes it absent.
Overwintering (basal) leaves are kept through the winter rather than shed. PATO's definition puts the disposition on the plant, not the leaf, so the fit is loose.

label: pseudowhorled
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being inserted singly but crowded on very short internodes, so that several appear to arise at one node as in a whorl. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0001951 whorled; not an approximate value of whorled, since the bearer is not whorled.
reason: A standard term for leaves or flowers that only look whorled. Mapping it to whorled, even as an approximate value, would assert a false arrangement.
Two values: spotted (PATO_0000333) with marks coloured red (PATO_0000322). Same pattern as 'marked with yellow'.
Barbed is already defined by backward-pointing projections, so 'retrorsely' adds nothing.
Paleae spirally ranked are inserted along a spiral round the receptacle.
A hyphenated compound of two orientation values: spreading (PATO_0104356) to reflexed (PATO_0104353).
sub- plus orbicular (PATO_0001934) with qualifier 'sub', exactly as 'suborbicular' in the pattern.
PATO caudate means having a tail or tail-like projection, so seeds or anthers without tails are not caudate.

'Inflorescences thyrses' gives the inflorescence architecture. PO splits thyrse into determinate (PO_0030128) and indeterminate (PO_0030127), and floras rarely say which, so the FLOPO value is the safe target.
Two values of one bearer: fringed (PATO_0040008) and the fringe white (PATO_0000323). A combined term would duplicate the colour scale.
Wide-ovate means broadly ovate, a kind of ovate. The width is a degree that the length-to-width ratio pattern (11) records when numbers are given.
Keeled maps to PATO keel-shaped (rule C221), and 'without keel' negates it. 'Abaxial' is the surface region of the bearer. PO keel (PO_0025327) is the papilionaceous petal pair and does not apply.
States that the rootstock or plant bears no tubers. The fragment 'or tubers' should be dropped.
Both values hold together, so it is not a continuum: the apex is acute (FLOPO:0991095) and ends in an awn (awn PO_0025349 present, as aristate).

target: callus-tipped (new class proposed for 'callus-pointed' in this batch)
reason: Same quality as callus-pointed. It should be one class with both words as synonyms, not two classes.
Both values hold together: conical (PATO_0002021) and ending abruptly in a short point (FLOPO:0991054 mucronate, the nearest term for apiculate).
